gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both diagnose that the stated C1 regularity of the velocity does not ensure existence of characteristics for all requested times, so the characteristic flow, evolved domains, and associated constructions may be undefined. ISSUE-003 also specifies the needed complete-flow hypothesis.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The paper uses a globally defined characteristic flow despite assuming only local continuous differentiability; finite-time escape can prevent the required all-time flow.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of the old C1 assumptions to guarantee a complete characteristic flow, including finite-time escape despite nonintersection.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly states that continuous first derivatives provide only local uniqueness, gives finite-time blowup as a counterexample, and distinguishes this from the required global trajectory existence.

component_coverage.gold_component: Consequent undefined characteristic-dependent domains and constructions, requiring a complete-flow assumption or equivalent growth condition.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the resulting nonexistence of upstream domains and characteristic test functions and proposes a complete-flow hypothesis with global bounds.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false unit-Jacobian and exact Lp-invariance premise in the characteristic change of variables. ISSUE-004 gives the same expanding-flow example and the determinant-based or divergence-based repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The characteristic map is generally compressible, so changing variables introduces a flow-Jacobian determinant; preserving the integration domain does not imply norm invariance.

component_coverage.gold_component: The flow displacement depends on the spatial point and the change of variables therefore has a non-unit Jacobian, with an explicit scaling counterexample.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 states that the flow Jacobian is not generally one, computes the scaling for A(x,t)=x, and notes that equality would require volume preservation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The same unit-Jacobian error affects moving bounded domains and requires determinant bounds rather than exact invariance.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 says both norm-invariance lemmas are false and repairs them by retaining the flow Jacobian and using upper and lower bounds.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both diagnose that the bounded-domain functional evaluates W at a flow-forward point that need not lie in G, without an extension or invariance assumption, so the functional is not defined for every W in L2(G).
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The characteristic composition is not a well-defined operation on H(G)=L2(G) when the flow does not map G into itself and no extension of W is supplied.

component_coverage.gold_component: The functional quantifies over W defined only on G but evaluates it outside G under the characteristic map.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly identifies the almost-everywhere domain limitation and the absence of a map-into-G or extension assumption.

component_coverage.gold_component: Consequently the bounded-domain functional is not well-defined, with a repair requiring correct source/target spaces or an extension.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 states that the functional is false as a general bounded-functional statement and proposes an extension or correctly connected source and target spaces.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid inference from L2 integrability or support equality to membership in the paper's strictly compactly supported H0 space. ISSUE-002 additionally explains the nonclosed-space problem and the resulting failure for ordinary elementwise DG functions, which is a broader presentation of the same support-membership defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed H0 definition requires compact containment of the support, but the L2 calculation and support equality for elementwise DG functions provide only square integrability or support up to the domain boundary, not H0 membership.

component_coverage.gold_component: Square integrability alone does not establish membership in the printed strictly compactly supported H0 space.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly distinguishes the L2 status from compact containment and notes that support equal to the domain or an element is not compactly contained there.

component_coverage.gold_component: The unsupported H0 inference propagates to remapped functions and later compact-support arguments, requiring a corrected space or support convention.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the false membership conclusion for characteristic-function-multiplied DG functions and proposes replacing H0 with an appropriate closed L2 or actual DG space and redoing the arguments.
